Use This Move To Scan The Play The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Ryan Leonard $84M Extension, Drake Batherson $86M Deal, and Shawn Horcoff Named DET Interim GM
videos.summary_source_text:
Ryan Leonard $84M Extension, Drake Batherson $86M Deal, and Shawn Horcoff Named DET Interim GM The latest episode of The Sheet with Jeff Marek covers a massive day of NHL news, including Ryan Leonard signing an eight-year, $84 million extension with the Washington Capitals, Drake Batherson agreeing to an eight-year, $86 million deal with the Ottawa Senators, Connor Bedard being named captain of the Chicago Blackhawks and Shawn Horcoff taking over as interim GM of the Detroit Red Wings.

Tarik El-Bashir joins Jeff to break down the Ryan Leonard extension, the Capitals' upcoming season and why NHL teams are getting more aggressive about locking up young RFAs early in the wake of major offer sheets around the league.

NHL player agent Matt Keator joins Jeff to discuss Chris Kreider signing with the Montreal Canadiens, the Leo Carlsson offer sheet from earlier this summer and the growing era of NHL player empowerment. videos.title: That Belly May Not Be Fat — Do This to Feel Lighter Fast | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
That Belly May Not Be Fat — Do This to Feel Lighter Fast | Dr. Mandell What you see on the scale—and even what you see in the mirror—isn’t always body fat. Changes in carbohydrate intake, glycogen storage, sodium, hydration, food choices, and digestion can influence body weight and how your body looks and feels. Glycogen stored in your muscles is associated with significant amounts of water, which helps explain why body weight can sometimes change surprisingly quickly when diet and activity change. In this video, Dr. Mandell explains how reducing highly processed foods and excess sodium, choosing potassium-rich whole foods such as fruits and vegetables, staying appropriately hydrated, getting physical activity, and improving the overall quality of your diet may help your body manage excess fluid and leave you feeling lighter. You’ll also learn about magnesium, hibiscus, dandelion, and the important relationship between sodium, potassium, glycogen, and water balance. Remember, rapid changes on the scale are generally not the same thing as rapid fat loss, and individual responses vary. People with kidney, heart, blood-pressure, or electrolyte problems, or those taking medications that affect fluid or potassium balance, should speak with their healthcare professional before making significant dietary or supplement changes. Make it a great day! — Dr. Alan Mandell

Despite being an excellent golfer, Iona was struggling with thin iron shots, poor compression and an inability to take a divot after the ball. The data revealed why: she was hitting two degrees up on her irons while swinging too far from the inside.

Rather than filling her head with technical swing thoughts, Piers and Andy gave Iona two simple external cues. By focusing on the shot she wanted to create and striking the ground beyond a line, her body naturally organised the movement she needed.

videos.title: Grok 5: Elon Musk Is Building Something Insane
videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 5: Elon Musk Is Building Something Insane Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Grok 4.7 was supposed to launch on September 11th, 2026. It didn’t. Just two days later, Elon Musk had already shifted the conversation to Grok 4.8 — and an even bigger model behind it: Grok 5.

xAI says Grok 5 is planned before the end of 2026, and Musk has claimed it will train on the entire SpaceX data corpus, covering more than 25 years of engineering records and employee output. But other eye-catching numbers surrounding the model — including a possible six trillion parameters and Musk’s earlier claim of a roughly 10% chance of AGI — are far less certain.

That distinction matters, because Grok 5 is already accumulating enormous expectations despite having no public architecture, context window, benchmark preview, or confirmed training-compute specification.

The hardware behind it, however, is much more concrete.

Colossus II is xAI’s massive Blackwell-generation expansion in Memphis. Plans discussed in the video point toward roughly 440,000 GB200 and GB300 GPUs in Colossus II alone. Combined with the existing campus, independent analysis puts the operation at roughly 555,000 GPUs and close to 2 gigawatts of power draw.

Then there’s the cost. GPU hardware alone is estimated at around $18 billion, while the complete infrastructure could potentially reach $35–58 billion once buildings, cooling, battery storage, and power systems are included.

So what does that amount of compute actually buy xAI?

Grok 5 could make a substantial jump in reasoning depth and context handling. Coding is less straightforward. Grok 4.6 trails its closest contemporaneous rival on Stanford’s APEX-SWE benchmark in the figures examined here, suggesting that simply adding parameters and compute may not be enough. Better software-engineering training data and reinforcement learning could matter just as much.

There’s also a multimodal catch. Grok currently relies on separate systems for capabilities such as image generation and voice rather than functioning as one unified model that natively handles every modality. Nothing publicly available confirms that Grok 5 changes that architecture.

And the competition isn’t standing still. This video looks at where Grok 5 could realistically land against OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, Google Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Anthropic’s latest Claude models — and why increasingly narrow benchmark gaps between frontier labs make claims of a dramatic category-defining lead harder to justify.

Finally, there’s Musk’s AGI framing. More compute can produce a significantly more capable model, but bigger context windows, stronger benchmarks, and longer reasoning chains do not automatically give a system autonomous learning, independent goal-setting, or self-improvement.

The most remarkable part of Grok 5 may therefore be the part that already exists: xAI has built an extraordinary amount of physical infrastructure around its next generation of models. Whether Grok 5 turns that investment into a genuine frontier-model breakthrough is still an open question.

CHAPTERS

01:42 The Grok 4.7 Disappearing Act
03:12 What xAI Has Actually Confirmed About Grok 5
04:29 Colossus II: The Machine That Would Train It
06:02 What That Compute Could Actually Buy
07:51 The Multimodal Reality Check
08:40 Where This Actually Lands Against the Competition
09:47 Is This Actually a Step Toward AGI
10:57 The Bottom Line

videos.title: 482. FIRE via tjänstepension: så slutade Johan jobba vid 55
videos.summary_source_text:
482. FIRE via tjänstepension: så slutade Johan jobba vid 55 Många är vi som drömmer om jobba mindre, resa mer och ha mer tid till det som är viktigt. Så var det även för Johan Strand som tack vare löneväxling, tjänstepension och väldigt medvetna val kunde gå i pension vid 55 år. 

Dagens avsnitt handlar om Johans resa från att ha varit en av pionjärerna inom svensk e-handel med datorbutiken.com, konkursen i samband med finanskrisen 2008, skilsmässa och ändå möjligheten att sluta jobba vid 55 år och leva ett rikt liv. Något han pratat om både i TV4:s nyhetsmorgon och DN.

Några av ämnena vi tar upp i veckans avsnitt är:

• Från konkurs och skilsmässa till pension vid 55, femton år senare

• Löneväxling till tjänstepension: Johans hemlighet

• Bolånelöftet är en fälla för många

• Är bostaden en investering? (vi har lite olika åsikt 🙈)

• En miljon kvar på kontot när du dör betyder att du sparat för mycket

• FIRE är en gammal idé i nya kläder: Diogenes, Thoreau och Strindberg

• De flesta jojo-sparar bara

• Hälften av oss får en bestående krämpa vid 68–69 års ålder

• Van life, Burning Van och livet efter att identiteten frikopplats från jobbet

Vi hoppas att du gillar avsnittet,
Jan, Caroline och Johan

Moving the body and arms as one unit is the single biggest reason high handicap golfers can't fix a slice or generate real golf club head speed — and most of them have no idea that's what they're doing. Eric Cogorno breaks down the exact three-part golf swing drill he used at his golf school to take a student from weak slices and zero confidence to hitting the best iron shot of his life — a high draw seven iron — within two days. The fix starts with learning how to release the golf club freely: lead arm folds, elbow slightly down, club re-hinges to 90 degrees. Then the trail foot pulls back to shut off excessive golf body rotation, and finally a slight in to out arm path eliminates the over the top move for good. These are the high handicap golf tips that actually change ball striking — not swing thoughts, not positions, but a free athletic arm swing that lets the club head speed take care of itself. If you leave this video without trying the lead arm fold drill, you're leaving two clubs of distance and a straight ball flight on the table.

• Why high handicap golfers move the body and arms as one unit — and why that kills golf club head speed and causes weak slices

• How to practice the lead arm fold drill on the tee box before every round to groove the correct release pattern
• Part two: how pulling the trail foot back closes the hip and shoulder to stop coming over the top and eliminate the slice
• Why keeping the shirt buttons behind the ball lets the arms swing freely past the body — the key to how to release the golf club correctly
• Part three: how adding a slight in to out arm path with the body closed fixes the slice and produces a consistent draw
• The complete three-part golf swing drill sequence any high handicap golfer can use to go from weak slices to high draws

videos.title: 14.09.26 - Ep.23 (Part 3) - Overconfidence Bias
videos.summary_source_text:
14.09.26 - Ep.23 (Part 3) - Overconfidence Bias In this episode, we continue exploring the psychology and biology behind financial decision-making and examine how elite traders think differently from the average market participant.

Success can build confidence, but repeated success can also create overconfidence. When traders begin to believe they understand the market better than they actually do, they may increase position sizes, use excessive leverage, and ignore risk. The same cycle can appear after losses, when traders attempt to recover quickly by taking larger and more dangerous positions.

We also explore herd mentality, the Dunning–Kruger effect, and how multiple cognitive biases can combine to create speculative bubbles. Confirmation bias, recency bias, FOMO, loss aversion, and overconfidence can reinforce one another until market prices become disconnected from fundamentals.

The episode then moves into the mindset of professional and elite traders. Rather than searching for certainty, professionals work with probabilities. They focus on expected value, risk-to-reward, portfolio exposure, and whether a potential loss can be absorbed. They understand that a good decision can produce a temporary loss, while a poor decision can sometimes produce a temporary profit.

Key concepts covered include:

Overconfidence bias and the dangers of excessive leverage
The overconfidence and loss-recovery loop
Herd mentality and crowd-driven market movements
The Dunning–Kruger effect
How cognitive biases combine to create speculative bubbles
Why intelligence alone does not guarantee trading success
Probabilities versus predictions
Process versus outcome
First-principles thinking
Bayesian thinking and updating decisions with new information
Capital preservation and avoiding unnecessary losses
How hedge funds and professional firms engineer discipline
Investment committees, risk reviews, position limits, and trading journals
Why elite traders rely on systems rather than emotion

The central lesson is simple: trading is not only about predicting what the market might do. It is about managing uncertainty, controlling risk, and repeatedly making informed decisions.

Discipline begins with self-awareness.

Watch, learn, take notes, and continue building your understanding of professional trading psychology through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series. Uncovering Three Keys to Matthews' Unique Movement The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Why Are AI CEOs Suddenly Saying “Slow Down”?
videos.summary_source_text:
Why Are AI CEOs Suddenly Saying “Slow Down”? Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Sam Altman and Dario Amodei now agree that frontier AI may need to slow down — but the strange part is that Altman was saying it before Amodei's essay was even published.

And this isn't just rhetoric. OpenAI reportedly paused parts of frontier training after GPT-6 Astra crossed its "Critical" cybersecurity capability threshold, while recent incidents at OpenAI, Hugging Face, and Anthropic exposed a much harder problem: the safety environments used to test increasingly capable AI agents aren't always as isolated as researchers thought.

On September 12, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published "We Must Pace the Frontier," arguing that AI labs should deliberately slow capability growth when safety, alignment, interpretability, security, and evaluations can't keep up. The apparent contradiction is hard to miss. Anthropic is simultaneously expanding compute, maintaining a rapid model cadence, and sitting on enormous infrastructure commitments.

But Amodei points to two developments that changed his thinking.

First, AI is becoming increasingly involved in the process of building better AI. Anthropic believes systems could automate or radically accelerate parts of frontier AI research as early as 2027. Second was the OpenAI–Hugging Face cybersecurity incident involving GPT-5.6 Sol and a more capable internal model.

During a controlled cyber evaluation, agents exploited a real vulnerability, gained network access, moved laterally, and interacted with actual Hugging Face infrastructure. METR later reported that roughly 1,200 supposedly isolated agents accessed an unauthorized shared communication channel, with hundreds participating in coordinated activity.

The important distinction is what the evidence does NOT show. There is no published evidence that these agents were trying to "escape," preserve themselves, or avoid shutdown. They had been instructed to perform offensive cybersecurity tasks. The more grounded concern is that capable agents can cross boundaries in flawed test environments and even interfere with the systems designed to evaluate them.

Anthropic discovered its own version of this problem after reviewing 141,006 cybersecurity evaluation runs. Three Claude evaluations touched real systems after supposedly isolated environments were accidentally connected to the live internet. Anthropic likewise found no evidence of deliberate self-exfiltration.

Then GPT-6 Astra reportedly crossed a capability line OpenAI hadn't faced before.

OpenAI classified Astra as reaching its "Critical" cybersecurity threshold: the level where a model could independently develop zero-day exploits against hardened targets or execute novel end-to-end attacks from high-level goals. OpenAI's response shows what "pacing" currently means in practice. Parts of frontier training were paused, safeguards were strengthened, and work resumed once OpenAI judged those protections sufficient.

So are the labs actually slowing down?

OpenAI has selectively done it. Anthropic's more concrete commitment is different: permanent independent evaluators with near-employee-level access. But neither company is proposing to simply stop developing frontier AI.

And that's where the prisoner's dilemma appears. One lab slowing while competitors continue racing risks sacrificing customers, investment, talent, and technological leadership. China complicates that calculation further, with companies including Z.ai and DeepSeek continuing to advance their own models.

Critics including Stuart Russell and David Krueger argue Amodei's proposal doesn't go far enough. Others question whether safety regulation could disproportionately burden startups and open developers while strengthening the largest frontier labs.

There are real commercial incentives here. There are also real safety incidents, real capability thresholds, and real costs being imposed by the labs on themselves.

What still doesn't exist is the crucial piece: a binding agreement between competitors. No shared training-rate limit. No universal capability checkpoint. No enforcement mechanism if one company decides to keep accelerating.

The AI industry may finally have real brakes. The question is whether anyone can afford to use them first.

videos.title: 10 Prompting Tricks That Make GPT-6 Astra INSANELY Powerful
videos.summary_source_text:
10 Prompting Tricks That Make GPT-6 Astra INSANELY Powerful Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

GPT-6 Astra is insanely powerful — but most people are still prompting it like GPT-4. And that means a flagship AI model with stronger reasoning, coding, and multi-step capabilities can still give you painfully generic answers.

The difference often comes down to just a few extra details.

Ask Astra to “help me plan a marketing campaign,” and you’ll likely get the usual advice: identify your audience, create content, track results. But give it a $5,000 budget, a two-month deadline, a 10% sales target, defined roles, and instructions to identify risks — and suddenly the same model has enough information to build something far more useful.

That’s the central idea behind this video: better prompting isn’t about writing enormous 500-word mega-prompts. It’s about giving GPT-6 Astra the information that actually changes the answer.

We break down a practical five-part framework for stronger prompts: goal, context, constraints, process or criteria, and output format. You won’t need every piece for every request, but this framework gives you a reliable way to diagnose why an AI response feels vague, generic, or disconnected from what you actually needed.

Then we put that framework to work.

We ask Astra to design a small 2D survival game for a solo beginner developer with only six weeks to build it. Instead of letting the model invent an impossibly ambitious game, the prompt forces it to consider scope, progression, survival mechanics, environmental threats, win conditions, and which features should be simplified or removed.

We also look at planning prompts, including how to turn a vague request for help organizing a virtual tech workshop into an actual three-month project plan with responsibilities, contingencies, and priorities if the budget gets cut.

But prompting gets even more useful when you stop asking AI to simply generate things.

If you want real critique instead of empty praise, you need to define what “better” actually means. If you want Astra to compare Trello, Asana, Notion, and Basecamp, you need to tell it whether cost, features, or learning curve matters most — especially when your team has a $50-per-month budget and isn't highly technical.

The same principle applies to brainstorming. “Give me 20 ideas” produces a pile of ideas that you still have to evaluate yourself. A better workflow separates generation from evaluation: brainstorm ideas, define criteria, score each option, select the strongest candidates, and only then build an execution plan.

And that's where GPT-6 Astra becomes much more useful: not as a machine that gives you one magical answer, but as something you can iteratively steer.

We demonstrate that with a $5,000 family trip to Italy. Instead of trying to engineer one perfect prompt, you can build an initial itinerary, add a required day in Milan, cut the budget by 20%, identify overloaded days, and finally convert the result into a screenshot-friendly checklist — all through short follow-up prompts.

The biggest mistake is assuming better prompting means longer prompting. It doesn't. Clear goals, relevant context, meaningful constraints, useful evaluation criteria, and the right output format matter far more.

And when Astra gets close but doesn't quite nail the answer? Don't throw everything away and start again. Keep steering.

videos.title: Did AI Doom Us All?
videos.summary_source_text:
Did AI Doom Us All? Are all of these AI safety campaigns part of a big coordinated psyop?

Apparently some people are actually being paid to push anti-AI messaging, but I’m not sure if that’s the case in these recent instances. 

I think it’s more likely that these Anthropic and OpenAI whistleblowers are usually from the alignment and safety sector, so their entire job is to study potential worst-case scenarios. Spending every day inside that world probably changes how you see the risks, but it also means they may be noticing dangers the rest of us aren’t.

I’m inclined to believe their warnings are genuine, but I don’t think panic is the answer. 

The AI arms race probably isn’t slowing down anytime soon. So maybe the smartest move is putting more brainpower into alignment and not just shareholder value.

What do you think: genuine warning or manufactured fear?

videos.title: Kimi wins, Lando loses out, but could Max have won? | Spanish GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast
videos.summary_source_text:
Kimi wins, Lando loses out, but could Max have won? | Spanish GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast Tom Clarkson is joined by journalists Albert Fabrega and Julianne Cerasoli to reflect on the first Spanish Grand Prix at the Madring circuit.

The Virtual Safety Car came at just the wrong time for race leader Lando Norris on lap 15, costing him victory after he’d made a great start from pole. Could McLaren have pre-empted the VSC? Why did Lando pit after the VSC ended? Could he have stayed out on the medium tyre?

Tom, Albert and Julianne discuss those talking points and you’ll hear reaction from McLaren Team Principal Andrea Stella.

Kimi Antonelli capitalised on Lando’s misfortune to take his eighth victory of the season and move 81 points clear of Mercedes teammate George Russell at the top of the World Championship.

And Max Verstappen came home in P2 for his sixth podium of the year. But could he have won the race if Red Bull hadn’t asked him to let Lewis Hamilton past after their opening lap incident?

Bedard Made This His Signature Shot The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

videos.title: Nikita Kucherov: Average Body, Extraordinary Skill
videos.summary_source_text:
Nikita Kucherov: Average Body, Extraordinary Skill The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: ChatGPT, Claude, Grok all DOWN, dangerous new AI models, Pentagon AI: AI NEWS
videos.summary_source_text:
ChatGPT, Claude, Grok all DOWN, dangerous new AI models, Pentagon AI: AI NEWS Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Three of the biggest AI systems went down on the same morning. Anthropic’s Claude started throwing elevated errors, xAI’s Grok went completely offline minutes later, and OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Codex followed. For over an hour, the incidents overlapped — immediately triggering theories about a coordinated cyberattack or a massive shared cloud failure.

But that’s not what the evidence shows.

OpenAI blamed a routing error. Anthropic cited an infrastructure issue affecting Claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and its API. SpaceX tied Grok’s outage to its Memphis compute center. Meanwhile, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Cloudflare showed normal operations. Even reports that Google Gemini had gone down were never confirmed by Google.

Three companies. Three different explanations. One very strange morning.

There is still an interesting complication. SpaceX operates compute infrastructure reportedly used by other AI companies, including Anthropic. That raises the possibility that apparently separate incidents could still expose how concentrated modern AI infrastructure has become. Nobody has confirmed that connection, and the companies haven’t released detailed postmortems, so major questions remain.

But the outages were only the beginning of a much bigger week.

On September 1, OpenAI revealed that its upcoming model, internally called Astra and expected to ship as GPT-6, had crossed into the “Critical” cybersecurity capability tier under its Preparedness Framework. In testing, Astra reportedly discovered two real, previously undocumented zero-day vulnerabilities autonomously.

OpenAI isn’t shelving the model. Instead, it plans to restrict initial access through a vetted group called Daybreak Blue, giving trusted testers and security partners access before any broader rollout.

Anthropic has made a strikingly similar decision.

Claude Fable 5.1 is publicly available and can identify software vulnerabilities, but according to Anthropic it cannot exploit them. The more capable Claude Mythos 5.1 is restricted to approved researchers working in cybersecurity and life sciences.

OpenAI and Anthropic use different safety frameworks, but both appear to be reaching the same conclusion: the most cyber-capable frontier AI models may no longer go directly from the lab to unrestricted public access.

Then there’s the Pentagon.

On August 31, the Department of Defense expanded GenAI.mil, its secure AI platform built for roughly three million DoD personnel. Google’s Gemini for Government was already integrated. Now ChatGPT Mil and Starshield AI’s Grok for Government are joining it.

The new systems are IL5 and CUI-certified and designed for controlled unclassified government work, including document drafting, planning, logistics, file handling, and acquisition support. More than 1.7 million people had reportedly enrolled on GenAI.mil by summer 2026, before the OpenAI and xAI additions went live.

OpenAI also signed a roughly $200 million Pentagon contract in June 2025 to develop government-grade AI tools.

But one major frontier lab is missing: Anthropic.

Claude’s absence reportedly follows the Trump administration designating Anthropic a “supply-chain risk” after a separate policy dispute, a designation Anthropic is challenging legally. That means access to one of the largest government AI deployments is increasingly being shaped not only by benchmarks and technical capabilities, but by policy.

Put these stories together and a bigger pattern emerges.

AI is becoming operational infrastructure while the systems themselves are becoming powerful enough that their creators are restricting access. At the same time, governments are deciding which frontier labs get plugged directly into enormous institutional deployments.

The conspiracy surrounding the outages wasn’t supported by the evidence. What actually happened may be more important: three major AI providers failed at nearly the same time for apparently different reasons, two competing labs independently decided their newest models needed restricted access, and the Pentagon picked its AI partners — while leaving one of the biggest names in AI outside the door.

09:15 Anthropic's Quieter Version of the Same Decision

The goal is simple: spend less time doing the easier reps that only get you to fatigue, and more time doing the hard, high-effort reps that are most responsible for stimulating new muscle growth.

To demonstrate how effective reps work, Jesse performs dumbbell bench press sets in two different styles. First, he performs a traditional set with a weight that causes failure somewhere around the 10 to 12 rep range. The first several reps are relatively easy. The real challenge doesn’t begin until the final reps, when effort rises sharply and every repetition becomes a grind.

Instead of resting two or three minutes and fully recovering before another traditional set, Jesse rests only about 15 to 30 seconds and gets right back into the dumbbell bench press. Because he has not fully recovered, he reaches those difficult reps almost immediately. Rather than spending another six or seven reps just trying to get back to the point where the set becomes hard, nearly every rep now demands a high level of effort.

This is a rest-pause style of training designed specifically for hypertrophy. It is not how I would train for maximal strength or power, where longer rest periods and high-quality reps are important. But if your goal is to build a bigger chest, increase muscle size, and make your chest workout more efficient, this technique gives you a new way to structure your sets.

The first set is what I call the ignition set. Choose a weight that makes you fail somewhere around 10 to 12 reps. That set gets you to the level of fatigue necessary to begin accumulating effective reps. After that, rest only 15 to 30 seconds, perform another set to failure, rest briefly again, and continue accumulating reps until you reach your target number.

For example, you might perform 20 effective reps on the dumbbell bench press. Your ignition set does not count toward those 20. After the short rest, you might get 5 effective reps, then 4, then 3, and continue chipping away until you reach 20 total effective reps. If your reps begin dropping to singles or doubles, reduce the weight slightly and continue.

This same strategy can be used to create an entire chest workout. You could perform 20 effective reps on the dumbbell bench press, move to an incline bench press to target the upper chest differently, then use cable crossovers, and finish with weighted or paused dips for another intense chest-building stimulus.

Instead of thinking only in terms of 3 sets of 10 or 4 sets of 12, you can begin programming your workout around the number of truly challenging reps you want to accumulate.

This can also help answer one of the most common questions lifters ask: how do I get a bigger chest when my current chest workout has stopped producing results? Sometimes the answer is not adding more exercises, more sets, or more total time in the gym. Sometimes it is changing the quality and effort of the reps you are already doing.

Effective reps require honest effort. If you stop a set too early, the entire method loses its purpose. With lighter weights and higher-rep sets, this becomes even more important because so many of the early repetitions are simply getting you closer to the reps that matter. If you choose a lighter weight, you still need to take the set close enough to true muscular failure for those final reps to become meaningful.

They talk about shortening the rest period, getting back into the hard reps faster, and how this style of training changed the way they think about building muscle.

If hot flashes and night sweats are just normal menopause symptoms, why do some women experience them before menopause, and others never experience them at all?

Hot flashes and night sweats are not the same. Hot flashes are related to the speed of a hormonal drop. A fast dip in estrogen can signal the hypothalamus, which has a thermostat that regulates body temperature. Stress can also contribute to hot flashes.

Genistein may be beneficial in blocking the receptors in the brain that trigger hot flashes and night sweats. Adequate magnesium levels are also important. 

Night sweats can last significantly longer than hot flashes, sometimes lasting up to an hour. Night sweats often happen between 3 and 4 a.m. and are more related to blood sugar than hormones. Addressing blood sugar, avoiding snacking at night, following a low-carb diet, and practicing intermittent fasting can help.

Are The New McLaren Blades Worth The HYPE? Rick puts the McLaren Series 1 bladed irons to the ultimate test to find out whether they deliver more than just the badge.

Bringing McLaren’s performance-driven Formula 1 philosophy into golf equipment, the Series 1 irons come with an astonishing price tag. But are they genuinely worth it? We put them head-to-head with arguably the best irons ever made to see whether McLaren can really compete at the highest level.

With McLaren Racing stars like Lando Norris representing the brand around the world, and CEO Zak Brown continuing to expand McLaren beyond motorsport, the Series 1 irons mark another bold move into a new performance arena. Developed with input from major champion Justin Rose, they combine striking premium looks with serious on-course technology and performance.

So, are McLaren genuine contenders capable of changing the golf equipment game, or is this simply a case of paying for the name?

Let us know what you think in the comments!

Kimchi + fried rice = sant! I Korea älskar man det här och rätten serveras i nästan alla restauranger och koreanska hem. Den härliga syran från kimchin tillsammans med hettan från gochujangen och krämigheten från ägget gör denna kombo oslagbart god!

2 portioner
20 minuter

1 gul lök
3 vitlöksklyftor
1 msk finhackad ingefära
½ msk gochujang
ca 6 dl kokt ris, gärna från dagen innan
2 dl kimchi, hackad 
2 ägg
2 salladslökar, tunt skivad
salt
rapsolja, och 25g smör till stekning

Topping:
Finhackad nori.
1 finhackad salladslök

1. Skala lök och vitlök. Finhacka löken och skiva vitlöken. Stek, lök, vitlök och ingefära i rapsolja i en stor stekpanna på medelhög värme i cirka 1 minut. 

2. Tillsätt gochujang och rör om. Hacka kimchin och blanda ner den tillsammans med riset. Fräs i några minuter, gå i med smör och smaka av med salt.

3. Stek äggen i en separat stekpanna. Toppa med salladslök och servera direkt.

Key to Scoring from Distance The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.summary_source_text:
Fattigvecka: att ta bort sina bekvämligheter i en vecka Fattigvecka: att ta bort sina bekvämligheter i en vecka för att skapa kontrast och uppskatta det man faktiskt har.

Vi pratade om det i avsnitt K64 för ett halvår sedan, och jag är supernyfiken på om någon faktiskt provade.

Så här kan det se ut:

- Sova på ett liggunderlag i stället för i sängen.
- Gå till jobbet i stället för att cykla eller ta bilen.
- Äta samma mat varje dag.
- Ta bort telefon och internet, gå till biblioteket för att använda datorn.

När Caroline och Jimmy som gjort FIRE pratade om det blev jag ganska avtänd. Samtidigt fattar jag poängen. Det kastar ljus på det som är viktigt.

Jimmy började skriva på en bok för att han blev så uttråkad av att vara utan internet, och skriva var precis det han velat göra mer av men aldrig hunnit. Caroline var efteråt helt lyrisk över sina skönhetsprodukter som hon inte använt under veckan.

Och ändå har jag svårt att motivera mig, trots att romarna och stoikerna pratade om precis det här för tusentals år sedan.

Har du provat eller känner du som mig?

- Gå till jobbet i stället för att cykla eller ta bilen.
- Äta samma mat varje dag.
- Ta bort telefon och internet, gå till biblioteket för att använda datorn.

När Caroline och Jimmy som gjort FIRE pratade om det blev jag ganska avtänd. Samtidigt fattar jag poängen. Det kastar ljus på det som är viktigt.

Jimmy började skriva på en bok för att han blev så uttråkad av att vara utan internet, och skriva var precis det han velat göra mer av men aldrig hunnit. Caroline var efteråt helt lyrisk över sina skönhetsprodukter som hon inte använt under veckan.

Och ändå har jag svårt att motivera mig, trots att romarna och stoikerna pratade om precis det här för tusentals år sedan.

Har du provat eller känner du som mig?

videos.title: Google Gemini Gems: 90% of Users Are Missing the Best Features
videos.summary_source_text:
Google Gemini Gems: 90% of Users Are Missing the Best Features Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Google Gems have changed dramatically since their original 2024 launch. What started as essentially a reusable prompt can now work with your own files, connect to Google Drive, be shared across teams, and act much more like a persistent, specialized AI assistant.

But there’s a major catch: not every Gemini user gets the same experience. Free accounts face a much smaller context window than paid tiers, which can become a serious limitation once you start loading large manuals, reports, policies, or other reference material into a Gem.

In this video, we rebuild Google Gems from the ground up and look at what has actually changed since launch — from expanded access and file-backed knowledge to sharing, Workspace integration, and newer automation capabilities. Then we build a Gem step by step so you can see which settings actually matter.

The instructions are where most Gems succeed or fail. Instead of giving Gemini a vague one-line prompt, we break the setup into four parts: persona, task, context, and format. We also cover the Knowledge panel, uploading or connecting reference files, knowledge citations, Google Drive requirements, the preview system, sharing permissions, and the Gem Manager.

More importantly, we look at the kinds of Gems that are actually worth building. A Personal Knowledge Base Gem can answer questions from your own policies and reports. A Brand Copywriter Gem can stay anchored to approved terminology and style guides. A shared Business Operations Gem can give an entire team a consistent source for policies and product information. And an Adaptive Tutor Gem can turn your own notes and slides into a personalized study system.

But building a Gem is only half the job.

Before trusting one, you need to test it with realistic prompts and deliberately look for places where its instructions break down. Gems can still misread uploaded material, lose useful context during longer conversations, and behave differently than expected when their instructions are underspecified.

There are structural limitations too. Free-tier context limits can become a problem with large documents, there’s a 10-file ceiling per Gem, conversation memory doesn’t automatically carry between sessions, Gemini Live isn’t supported, and multi-Gem workflows still require manual work. Real-time web access also depends on the extensions and capabilities available to your account rather than simply telling a Gem to search.

So if you built a Gem back when the feature first launched and dismissed it as a saved prompt with a fancy name, it may be worth rebuilding rather than simply reusing it. The biggest upgrade isn’t the name or interface — it’s giving a specialized assistant the right instructions, your actual reference material, and a repeatable job.

If You Need Perfect Feet To Shoot, You're Already Behind The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Use This Effortless Swing Tip To Hit Irons Further
videos.summary_source_text:
Use This Effortless Swing Tip To Hit Irons Further Want to hit the golf ball further but struggle to make a longer backswing?

In this Danny Maude golf lesson, you’ll learn how to create more distance without needing a huge golf swing.

This is particularly useful for golfers with limited mobility, golfers recovering from injury, senior golfers, or anyone who simply feels more comfortable making a shorter backswing.

Using one of Danny Maude’s favourite golf drills, this golf instruction video shows you how to improve your strike, create more clubhead speed and learn how to “catapult” the golf club through impact so you can generate effortless power with the swing you already have.

In this golf lesson, you’ll learn:

• How to hit the golf ball further with a short backswing
• Why you don’t need a longer golf swing to create more distance
• The finish position that helps improve ball striking
• Why the trail shoulder is so important through impact
• How to stop lunging towards the golf ball
• How to create more clubhead speed without swinging harder
• The “Longest Putt” golf drill for effortless power
• How to use sound to improve golf swing acceleration
• Why a shorter golf swing can improve your strike
• How to transfer this feeling into your full swing and driver

If you struggle with golf distance because your golf swing feels short, restricted or powerless, this is a brilliant golf drill to practise.

The key to hitting irons longer isn’t simply making a bigger backswing. It’s learning how to organise the body correctly, improve the quality of your strike and accelerate the golf club at the right moment through impact. This simple golf tip is incredible if you struggle to make a full golf swing. Danny helps many senior golfers hit driver straight while also helping them hit driver longer. This is one of his go to golf tips.

I’m going to share a natural remedy you may find helpful if you’re dealing with numbness, tingling, or a burning sensation in your feet.

Your tingling feet aren’t actually a nerve problem. If you have high blood sugar, there’s an increased demand for vitamin B1 because vitamin B1 is needed for sugar metabolism in the body.

High blood sugar means the tiny blood vessels around the nervous system aren’t getting enough energy. A vitamin B1 deficiency can mean low energy and lactic acid buildup.
Benfotiamine, a fat-soluble form of vitamin B1, can help with tingling and numbness in the feet. Take the recommended dose 3 to 4 times per day. 

Changing your diet is key to addressing the root cause of peripheral neuropathy. A low-carb diet can provide the body with ketones as an alternative fuel, helping properly fuel the neurons despite insulin resistance.

Peripheral neuropathy can also be linked to high vitamin B6 levels or low magnesium levels.

When you're eating frequently and choosing modern processed, high glycemic foods, insulin stays elevated for longer than it should. That's one of the reasons fasting can help lower insulin and improve metabolic health.
